cards.title: Timed Up and Go (TUG)
cards.note: CDC STEADI cutoff. Published cutoffs range from 12 to 16 s. Shuffling, en bloc turning or steadying on walls may signal a neurological problem worth further evaluation.
cards.tags: tug mobility gait steadi screen

cards.title: 30-second chair stand
cards.note: A below-average score (fewer stands than shown) indicates fall risk. Arms crossed, 17-inch seat; if the patient must use their arms, the score is 0.
cards.tags: 30s cst sit to stand chair rise strength norms steadi

cards.title: 4-Stage Balance Test
cards.note: Feet together, semi-tandem, tandem, single leg: 10 s each, no assistive device, eyes open. Unable to hold tandem for 10 s = increased fall risk.
cards.tags: 4 stage four stage tandem stance static balance steadi

cards.title: Berg Balance Scale
cards.note: The 45 cutoff misses about a third of fallers. Better: fall history + Berg < 51, or no history + Berg < 42 (91% sensitive, 82% specific). MDC depends on starting score; see the source for other ranges.
cards.tags: bbs berg static dynamic balance

cards.title: Gait speed
cards.note: Often called the sixth vital sign. Change estimates are from community-dwelling older adults; values after hip fracture run higher (0.10–0.17 m/s for small change).
cards.tags: gait speed walking speed 10mwt 4m walk sixth vital sign

cards.title: 6MWT & SPPB change
cards.note: Best initial estimates of meaningful change in older adults.
cards.tags: 6mwt six minute walk sppb short physical performance battery endurance

cards.title: Exercise (all types)
cards.note: 59 trials, 12,981 people. Larger effect when delivered by a health professional, usually a physical therapist.
cards.tags: exercise fall prevention cochrane

cards.title: Balance + functional training
cards.note: Mainly balance and functional exercises (sit-to-stand, stepping). Programs combining balance/functional + resistance: −34% (moderate certainty).
cards.tags: balance functional training resistance strength multicomponent

cards.title: Tai chi
cards.note: 9 trials. A good option to refer to once a patient finishes PT.
cards.tags: tai chi community program

cards.title: Otago Exercise Programme
cards.note: Home-based strength and balance program. 7 trials, 1,503 people, mean age 81.6. Rate ratio 0.68 for falls; risk ratio 0.45 for death.
cards.tags: otago home exercise program hep

cards.title: How much exercise
cards.note: Balance must be challenging and progressed. Continue longer for a greater effect; benefits fade within 3–6 months of stopping.
cards.tags: dose dosage frequency hours per week progression detraining

cards.title: World Falls Guidelines 2022
cards.note: Exercise: balance-challenging and functional, 3+ sessions a week, individualized, progressed for at least 12 weeks.
cards.tags: guideline wfg world falls montero-odasso grade

cards.title: Walking-only, resistance-only, dance
cards.note: Not enough evidence that programs mainly of walking, resistance, dance or flexibility prevent falls. Brisk walking alone is best avoided as a falls program.
cards.tags: walking program resistance only dance flexibility ineffective

cards.title: Orthostatic hypotension
cards.note: Or dizziness, lying to standing. Measure after 5 min supine, then at 1 and 3 min standing. Raises fall risk about 73%; flag it to the physician.
cards.tags: orthostatic postural hypotension blood pressure dizziness

cards.title: Medications & vision
cards.note: Flag psychoactive drugs, opioids, and anything sedating or lowering blood pressure for physician review. Deprescribing high-risk drugs can cut fall injuries by about 35%.
cards.tags: medications polypharmacy frid deprescribing vision eye

cards.title: Who is likely to fall
cards.note: Predictors of falls over 4 years. Simply asking about fear of falling works. About 1 in 3 community-dwelling adults 65+ fall each year; about half of nursing home residents.
cards.tags: risk factors prognosis fear of falling history incidence

cards.title: ACR clinical criteria, knee OA
cards.note: Age > 50, morning stiffness < 30 min, crepitus, bony tenderness, bony enlargement, no palpable warmth. In a general population the criteria do worse (41% sensitive, 75% specific) and mostly catch later disease.
cards.tags: acr altman criteria classification diagnosis crepitus

cards.title: OARSI performance tests
cards.note: Recommended set for hip and knee OA. For 30s chair stand norms by age, see the Falls hub.
cards.tags: oarsi core set performance tests 40m fast paced walk stair climb

cards.title: 30-second chair stand change
cards.note: Measured in hip OA; commonly applied to knee OA too.
cards.tags: 30s cst chair stand mcid mcii change

cards.title: 6-minute walk (OA)
cards.note: Hip or knee OA before joint replacement. A change smaller than this may be measurement error.
cards.tags: 6mwt six minute walk mdc arthroplasty

cards.title: Exercise
cards.note: First-line for nearly everyone with knee OA. No single exercise type is superior; benefit lasts up to a year.
cards.tags: exercise strengthening aerobic acr arthritis foundation

cards.title: Weight loss
cards.note: For patients who are overweight or obese. Even 5% gives a notable improvement in knee pain.
cards.tags: weight loss obesity bmi

cards.title: Tai chi, self-management, cane, brace
cards.note: Tai chi benefit lasts at least 24 weeks.
cards.tags: tai chi self efficacy self management cane brace balance

cards.title: After TKA: what the APTA guideline backs
cards.note: NMES to improve quadriceps strength. A 2025 revision of this guideline is in progress.
cards.tags: tka total knee arthroplasty replacement nmes strength post-op

cards.title: TENS
cards.note: Does not improve pain or function in knee OA.
cards.tags: tens electrical stimulation modality

cards.title: Arthroscopy for degenerative knees
cards.note: Applies to nearly all patients with knee OA or degenerative meniscal tears; no better than exercise therapy.
cards.tags: arthroscopy surgery meniscus menisectomy debridement

cards.title: Also recommended against
cards.note: ACR/Arthritis Foundation 2019.
cards.tags: manual therapy glucosamine chondroitin prp stem cell injection

cards.title: CPM after TKA
cards.note: Continuous passive motion devices are not recommended for primary TKA.
cards.tags: cpm continuous passive motion tka

cards.title: When it doesn't look like OA
cards.note: OA criteria assume no palpable warmth and morning stiffness under 30 minutes. A warm joint or long morning stiffness points away from OA; consider an inflammatory cause and refer.
cards.tags: inflammatory warmth stiffness referral

cards.title: Quadriceps weakness after TKA
cards.note: Pain and self-reported function improve after TKA, but quadriceps weakness and functional limits often persist. That is why strengthening (and NMES) matters.
cards.tags: tka quadriceps weakness prognosis outcome

cards.title: Lumbar spinal stenosis: best findings
cards.note: Older adults with leg pain. Wide-based gait has a very wide confidence interval (1.9–95). Combinations work best for ruling stenosis out.
cards.tags: lss spinal stenosis neurogenic claudication likelihood ratio romberg

cards.title: Stenosis cluster (Cook 2011)
cards.note: Bilateral symptoms; leg pain more than back pain; pain walking/standing; relief sitting; age > 48. Four of five gives a 76% post-test probability.
cards.tags: stenosis cluster cook clinical prediction rule

cards.title: Meaningful change in LBP
cards.note: International consensus values; treat as a starting point, not a fixed rule.
cards.tags: nprs oswestry odi roland morris rmdq mcid mic

cards.title: Older adults, chronic LBP
cards.note: General exercise training to reduce pain and disability.
cards.tags: exercise older adults chronic low back pain cpg

cards.title: Acute LBP
cards.note: Exercise training, including specific trunk muscle activation.
cards.tags: acute low back pain exercise trunk activation

cards.title: Cancer: history matters most
cards.note: The single most useful red flag for spinal malignancy. Most other red flags barely change the probability on their own; don't rely on any one question.
cards.tags: red flag malignancy cancer metastasis screening

cards.title: Spinal fracture
cards.note: Raise suspicion: older age, prolonged corticosteroid use, severe trauma, a contusion or abrasion.
cards.tags: fracture compression osteoporosis steroids trauma red flag

cards.title: Expected course
cards.note: Most improvement happens in the first six weeks, then slows. Useful for setting expectations with patients.
cards.tags: prognosis natural history recovery timeline
